name: Tag
description: A removable, categorisation label. Supports an optional leading icon slot and an optional close button for removal. Built for use in tag inputs, filter chips, and multi-select displays.

notes: The remove button receives aria-label='Remove {children}' to clearly communicate its action.
The icon slot is aria-hidden to prevent redundant announcements.
When onRemove is provided, the close button is focusable and keyboard-operable.

variant.description: Colour palette variant of the tag.

onRemove.description: When provided, renders a close button that triggers this callback (unless closeable is false). The button receives aria-label='Remove {children}'.

closeable.description: Whether the close button is visible when onRemove is provided. Set to false to hide the close button.

clickable.description: When true, the tag behaves as a toggle chip. The tag becomes clickable and receives role='option' and tabIndex=0.

isChecked.description: Whether the tag is currently in a checked/selected state. Only relevant when clickable is true. Controls aria-selected and visual checked style.

icon.description: An optional icon rendered at the inline-start of the label.

children.description: The label content of the tag.

className.description: Additional CSS class names to apply to the root element.

variants.neutral: Default style. Muted background, default text colour.
variants.primary: Highlighted style. Uses primary action token colours.
variants.info: Informational style. Uses info feedback tokens.
variants.success: Positive style. Uses success feedback tokens.
variants.warning: Caution style. Uses warning feedback tokens.
variants.danger: Error or critical style. Uses danger feedback tokens.

do: Use tags to represent user-selected filter values or categories.
Provide onRemove when the tag should be dismissible.
Keep tag labels concise — one to three words.
dont: Do not use tags for navigation — use links instead.
Do not nest interactive elements inside a tag beyond the close button.
Do not use tags as the only mechanism to communicate a state — pair with text.
